notes:
disagreement: cells: one pass tests assignment_group_id = 67 on the transferred cases, the other leaves the group untested; kept the tighter cell because the policy's assignment rule keeps the case's group and adds the assignee to it, and the benchmark's membership check adds Mendez to group 67, which only makes sense if the cases stay there.
disagreement: form: one pass tests the transfer as one set (cases 251 and 1142, expected 2), the other as one anchored requirement per case; chose one requirement per case so that each benchmark check is carried by its own requirement and each case is scored on its own.
The deactivation, the group removal and the group addition are not asked for in the request; they follow from the policy's leaving-employee rule and its rule that an assignee outside the case's group is added to it, and a listed tool covers each. The acting user (user 5) is an agent; the policy's default is to act with an admin's responsibilities, so deactivating Bullock and changing group memberships are in scope. The request names the departing teammate with 'he'; the user record is unambiguous (user 3 is the only Tabitha or Bullock). 'This is critical for our operations' describes the urgency of the request and asks no change to the cases' priority. The notifications' status and knowledge_id are fixed by neither the request nor the policy and are not tested.
